import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 101

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/101](https://www.erdosproblems.com/101)
-/



namespace Erdos101

open EuclideanGeometry Filter Asymptotics

/--
The set of lines in $\mathbb{R}^2$ containing exactly $k$ points from a given set $S$.
-/
private noncomputable def linesWithPointsFor (k : ℕ) (S : Set ℝ²) : Set (AffineSubspace ℝ ℝ²) :=
  let determined_lines := { affineSpan ℝ {p, q} | (p ∈ S) (q ∈ S) (_ : p ≠ q) }
  { L ∈ determined_lines | (↑L ∩ S).ncard = k }

/--
The maximum number of lines containing exactly $4$ points among all sets $S$ of $n$
points in $\mathbb{R}^2$ satisfying the condition that no five points are collinear.
-/
noncomputable def numLinesWithFourPointMax (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup {((linesWithPointsFor 4 S).ncard)| (S : Set ℝ²)
    (_ : S.ncard = n) (_ : S.Finite) (_ : NonCollinearFor 5 S)}

/--
Given $n$ points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, no five of which are on a line, the number of
lines containing four points is $o(n^2)$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 52]
theorem erdos_101 : (fun n => (numLinesWithFourPointMax n : ℝ)) =o[atTop] (fun n => (n : ℝ)^2) := by
  sorry

-- TODO(firsching): formalize other results from the additional material

end Erdos101

reformulations.difference: The source bounds the number of four-point lines in arbitrary admissible configurations; Lean states little-o growth of the supremum of those counts for each n.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For finite S, its determined lines form a finite subset of the image of S × S, so their count is at most |S|². Thus the supremum is bounded and bounds every admissible count. Conversely, a common bound on all admissible counts bounds the supremum. Consequently the Lean statement is equivalent to: for every ε > 0, there exists N such that every admissible n-point set with n ≥ N has at most εn² four-point lines. This equivalence was proved without sorry in /workspace/review/geometry_checks.lean as source_form_equiv.

reformulations.difference: For the k = 4 instance used in the file, Lean counts only lines obtained as affine spans of two distinct points of S, rather than starting with all geometric lines.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Any geometric line containing exactly four points of S contains two distinct such points, whose affine span equals that line. Conversely, the span of two distinct points is a geometric line. Set cardinality counts each line once regardless of the witnessing pair. The equivalence was proved for every k ≥ 2 as geometric_lines_iff; the helper's unused k = 0 and k = 1 cases do not affect the problem.
